calendarDiscovery.crawlerNotes: All three local two-page PDFs were fully extracted and visually inspected; current official downloads match by SHA-256. All are 2026-2027 variants, not successive years. The main calendar page is a JavaScript shell with no readable links; direct retrieval timed out even after an approved retry. Current official PDFs and the full official newsroom, January 23, 2025 adoption announcement, August 11, 2026 opening notice and September 3 Labor Day notice were checked. No later 2026-2027 operational change was verified. The adoption announcement independently confirms November 23-25 student Fall Recess for Elementary/Secondary and Adult/Vocational, resolving the employee-focused PDF wording. Do not transfer those dates to Juvenile Justice. Employee opt days are not student make-up reserves. Technical/adult planning days carry a principal-authorized class-swap exception. Wednesday one-hour release applies only to elementary grades 2-5 and K-8 center grades 2-8. Juvenile Justice includes 15 explicit Saturdays and two required summer grading periods. No future-year calendar was verified. schoolAgePopulation is an unset ranking placeholder, not enrollment.

faqs.question: Which Miami-Dade school calendar should I use?
faqs.answer: Use Elementary and Secondary for the regular district school schedule. Technical Colleges and Adult Education Centers have a longer trimester year. The Juvenile Justice Center uses a separate year-round calendar with summer grading periods and Saturday classes. Confirm independently operated charter-school and individual program schedules directly.

faqs.question: Are the three Miami-Dade calendars for different school years?
faqs.answer: All three calendars here are for 2026-2027. Their different ending dates reflect different programs. A 2027-2028, 2028-2029 or 2029-2030 calendar has not been verified here.

about.dataSource: The district-published 2026-2027 Elementary and Secondary calendar supplies the dates and program scope. Its two pages include the monthly grid, date explanations and scheduling footnotes. The official PDF is linked above alongside the district calendar page.
about.processing: All six pages across the three program PDFs were visually checked. This regular calendar contains only its own student-relevant dates; staff hiring, opt-work alternatives and pre/post-year planning are omitted. November 23-25 student status is confirmed by the January 23, 2025 official adoption announcement. The weekly Wednesday rule is expanded only onto actual attendance Wednesdays, with grade scope preserved. The grid reconciles to 180 days: 211 weekdays minus 31 no-class weekdays. Academic boundaries do not imply a student holiday. No 2026-2027 final-day early-dismissal announcement was verified; the newsroom’s last-three-days notice concerns 2025-2026 and is not transferred.
about.updates: Official PDF downloads and available district announcements were checked October 19, 2026. Check the district calendar page and school messages for later changes.
about.disclaimer: Use the calendar for the student’s own school or program. Building access, transportation, childcare and individual course meeting times should be confirmed with the school.

faqs.question: When does school start in Miami-Dade in 2026?
faqs.answer: Elementary and secondary students begin Thursday, August 13, 2026. This is also the beginning of the first semester.

faqs.question: What is the last day of school in Miami-Dade for 2026-2027?
faqs.answer: The last day for elementary and secondary students is Thursday, June 3, 2027. It also ends the fourth grading period and second semester. June 4 is a staff planning day.

faqs.question: When is Thanksgiving break in Miami-Dade?
faqs.answer: Students have no classes November 23-27, 2026. Fall Recess is November 23-25, Thanksgiving Day is November 26, and the Friday recess is November 27. Classes resume Monday, November 30; the surrounding weekends make a nine-day stretch from November 21-29.

faqs.question: When is Miami-Dade winter break, and when do students return?
faqs.answer: Winter Recess is December 21, 2026-January 1, 2027. Students are also off on the December 18 planning day. The last class before the break is Thursday, December 17, and classes resume Monday, January 4.

faqs.question: When is Miami-Dade spring break in 2027?
faqs.answer: Spring Recess is March 22-26, 2027. Monday, March 29 is a separate teacher planning day with no student classes, so students return Tuesday, March 30. Including the weekends, the continuous time away runs March 20-29.

faqs.question: Which students leave early on Wednesdays?
faqs.answer: The one-hour early-release rule covers elementary school students in grades 2-5 and K-8 center students in grades 2-8. It applies on Wednesdays when classes are held. Kindergarten and first grade are not included in this rule, and it is not a general early-release schedule for all secondary schools.

faqs.question: What time should I pick up my child on an early-release Wednesday?
faqs.answer: For the grades covered by the Wednesday rule, dismissal is one hour before the school’s regular dismissal time. The annual calendar does not give a clock time. Confirm pickup, bus and after-school arrangements with the school.

faqs.question: Which teacher planning days have no school for students?
faqs.answer: During the student year, classes are not held September 21, November 3 and December 18, 2026, or January 15, March 10 and March 29, 2027. November 3 is also a district-wide professional learning day.

faqs.question: Is there school on Labor Day or Veterans Day?
faqs.answer: No. Labor Day, September 7, and Veterans Day, November 11, 2026, are student holidays. The district’s Labor Day notice also closes schools and offices and announces reopening September 8.

faqs.question: Are students off for Martin Luther King Jr. Day and Presidents Day?
faqs.answer: Yes. Students are off Monday, January 18, 2027, for Martin Luther King Jr. Day and Monday, February 15, for All Presidents Day. January 15 is also a student-free planning day, creating a four-day January weekend.

faqs.question: Is Memorial Day a school day in 2027?
faqs.answer: No. Monday, May 31, 2027, is a student holiday. The school year continues afterward and ends June 3.

faqs.question: When does the second semester begin?
faqs.answer: The first semester ends Thursday, January 14, 2027. Students have no classes January 15 or January 18. The second semester begins Tuesday, January 19, with the third grading period.

faqs.question: When do Miami-Dade grading periods end?
faqs.answer: The four grading periods end October 16, 2026; January 14, March 19 and June 3, 2027. The next periods begin October 19, January 19 and March 30. These academic boundaries do not by themselves mean students leave early or miss class.

faqs.question: How many student days are on this calendar?
faqs.answer: The elementary and secondary calendar prints 180 days total. Its four grading periods list 45, 46, 42 and 47 days. The covered grades’ Wednesday early releases remain attendance days.

faqs.question: Does “available to opt” mean my child can choose whether to attend?
faqs.answer: No. That notation describes employee workday options. The associated teacher planning dates are still listed as having no students in school; they are not optional student attendance days.

faqs.question: Are hurricane make-up days listed for 2026-2027?
faqs.answer: The elementary and secondary PDF does not designate specific hurricane make-up dates. Employee opt-work dates are not a student make-up calendar. Follow district and school messages if weather changes the attendance schedule.

faqs.question: Will students leave early on the last day of school?
faqs.answer: The 2026-2027 annual calendar does not announce a special June 3 dismissal time. The Wednesday rule does not establish a Thursday early dismissal. Check the school’s end-of-year notice before changing pickup plans.

faqs.question: Where can I find report cards, testing dates and graduation details?
faqs.answer: This annual calendar gives grading-period boundaries, but it does not provide report-card release dates, a testing timetable or graduation ceremonies. Check the Parent Portal and school notices for those details.

faqs.question: Does this schedule also apply to technical colleges and the Juvenile Justice Center?
faqs.answer: Those programs have separate 2026-2027 calendars. Technical colleges and adult education centers continue through July 28. The Juvenile Justice Center includes summer grading periods and Saturday classes and runs through June 29.

editorialSummary.heading: The regular school year, with Wednesday pickup changes
paragraphs: Miami-Dade’s elementary and secondary school year begins Thursday, August 13, 2026, and ends Thursday, June 3, 2027. Wednesday pickup needs a separate reminder for families with children in elementary grades 2-5 or K-8 center grades 2-8: those students leave one hour before their usual dismissal time whenever Wednesday classes are held. The rule does not cover kindergarten, first grade or every middle and high school student. Ask the school for the actual pickup time before arranging transportation or after-school care.

Students have the full week of November 23-27 off, combining Fall Recess, Thanksgiving Day and the Friday recess. The winter recess itself runs December 21-January 1, but December 18 is also a student-free planning day, so the last class before the break is December 17. Classes resume January 4. Spring Recess runs March 22-26; a separate planning day on March 29 keeps students out until Tuesday, March 30. The first semester ends January 14, with a planning day and the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday before the second semester opens January 19.

faqs.question: When does the 2026-2027 technical and adult education year begin?
faqs.answer: The published first day is Thursday, August 13, 2026, beginning the first trimester. Ask your center for your own course’s meeting dates and session times.

faqs.question: When is the last day for Miami-Dade technical colleges and adult education centers?
faqs.answer: The calendar’s last student day is Wednesday, July 28, 2027, which also ends the third trimester. July 29 is a staff planning day.

faqs.question: What are the trimester dates?
faqs.answer: The first trimester runs August 13-December 17, 2026. The second runs January 4-April 16, 2027, and the third April 19-July 28. Holidays and planning days fall within these ranges; they are not uninterrupted daily class sessions.

faqs.question: How many instructional days does the technical and adult calendar list?
faqs.answer: The PDF prints 216 days total, with 82 days in the first trimester, 65 in the second and 69 in the third. This is the program calendar’s total, not a promise that every course meets on all 216 dates.

faqs.question: Are adult education students off for the full Thanksgiving week?
faqs.answer: Yes. The district’s adoption announcement confirms student Fall Recess November 23-25, 2026, for adult and vocational programs. Thanksgiving Day on November 26 and the November 27 recess complete the week. The published return is Monday, November 30.

faqs.question: When is winter recess for technical and adult education students?
faqs.answer: Winter Recess is December 21, 2026-January 1, 2027. The published schedule also has no student classes on the December 18 planning day, and the second trimester begins January 4. Adult education students should confirm any center-authorized planning-day class swap.

faqs.question: When do classes resume after spring recess?
faqs.answer: Spring Recess is March 22-26, 2027. March 29 is a planning day, so the standard published schedule resumes Tuesday, March 30. A center may announce a different adult education arrangement under the planning-day exchange rule.

faqs.question: Can an adult education center hold classes on a teacher planning day?
faqs.answer: Yes, at the principal’s discretion. When day-school activities disrupt an on-campus adult education program, classes may be held on a planning day instead of another regularly scheduled class day. Confirm the actual exchange with your center; the calendar does not assign a replacement date.

faqs.question: Which planning dates should technical and adult education students check with their center?
faqs.answer: The standard schedule lists no student classes September 21, November 3 and December 18, 2026, and January 15, March 10, March 29 and June 4, 2027. The adult education class-swap provision can affect a center’s arrangements on a planning day.

faqs.question: Do classes stop when the regular Miami-Dade school year ends in June?
faqs.answer: This program calendar continues after the elementary and secondary June 3 last day. June 4 is a published planning day, and the third trimester continues through July 28, subject to the center’s course schedule.

faqs.question: Which June and July holidays fall during the third trimester?
faqs.answer: Friday, June 18, 2027, is the Juneteenth observance, and Monday, July 5, is the Independence Day observance. Both are student holidays on this calendar.

faqs.question: Which other legal holidays have no student classes?
faqs.answer: The calendar lists Labor Day on September 7, Veterans Day on November 11, Thanksgiving on November 26, Martin Luther King Jr. Day on January 18, All Presidents Day on February 15 and Memorial Day on May 31. Recess and planning days are listed separately.

faqs.question: Does the Wednesday one-hour early-release rule apply to adult and technical students?
faqs.answer: That rule appears on the elementary and secondary calendar for specific elementary and K-8 grades. It is not a technical college or adult education dismissal rule. Use your center’s class schedule for daytime and evening sessions.

faqs.question: Does “available to opt” make attendance optional for students?
faqs.answer: No. The notation concerns employee workday choices. The separate principal-authorized adult education class-swap rule is what may change a center’s actual attendance arrangement.

faqs.question: Where can I find course times, registration deadlines and completion ceremonies?
faqs.answer: The district’s annual calendar does not set those details for every course or center. Contact your technical college or adult education center for the session timetable, enrollment deadlines and any program completion ceremony.

faqs.question: Where are the official adult education calendar and schedule changes posted?
faqs.answer: Download the Technical Colleges and Adult Education Centers PDF from this page or the district Calendars page. Confirm center-specific class exchanges directly and follow district messages for emergency schedule changes.

faqs.question: When does the Juvenile Justice Center’s 2026-2027 calendar begin and end?
faqs.answer: Summer 1 opens July 2, 2026, and Summer 2 ends June 29, 2027. Those are the first and final student-period dates on this year-round calendar. The first semester starts later, on August 19.

faqs.question: What are the two summer grading periods?
faqs.answer: Summer 1 runs July 2-August 18, 2026. Summer 2 runs May 17-June 29, 2027. Each has 30 days in the calendar’s published count. Holidays and student-free planning dates interrupt these periods, so the ranges are not a promise of class every day.

faqs.question: Does this program have school on Saturdays?
faqs.answer: Yes. The calendar lists 15 Saturday-school dates: August 22; September 12 and 26; October 10 and 24; November 7; December 12, 2026; January 9 and 23; February 6 and 27; March 13; April 10 and 24; and May 8, 2027. These dates apply to the Juvenile Justice Center program.

faqs.question: How many student days are on the Juvenile Justice Center calendar?
faqs.answer: The PDF prints 240 days total. The six periods list 30, 45, 42, 46, 47 and 30 days, including the two summer periods and scheduled Saturday classes.

faqs.question: Is the Juvenile Justice Center off for the full Thanksgiving week?
faqs.answer: No. November 23 and 24, 2026, are not marked as recess on this calendar. Students have no classes November 25 for teacher planning, November 26 for Thanksgiving and November 27 for recess. The published schedule resumes Monday, November 30.

faqs.question: When is winter recess, and when does the third grading period begin?
faqs.answer: Winter Recess is December 21, 2026-January 1, 2027. December 18 is also a planning day with no students. The third grading period and second semester begin Monday, January 4.

faqs.question: When is spring recess for the Juvenile Justice Center?
faqs.answer: Spring Recess is March 22-26, 2027. Students are also off for planning on March 29, giving a published return of Tuesday, March 30. March 13 is a scheduled Saturday class before the break.

faqs.question: Which August planning dates have no student classes?
faqs.answer: Students have no classes August 10, 11 or 12, 2026. August 11 is also district-wide professional learning. Summer 1 continues afterward through August 18, and the first grading period begins August 19.

faqs.question: Which other planning days are student days off?
faqs.answer: The calendar lists no student classes September 21, November 3, November 25 and December 18, 2026, and January 15, March 10 and March 29, 2027. November 3 is also district-wide professional learning.

faqs.question: What are the semester dates for this program?
faqs.answer: The first semester begins August 19 and ends December 17, 2026. The second begins January 4 and ends May 14, 2027. Summer 1 comes before those semesters, and Summer 2 follows them.

faqs.question: When do the four regular grading periods end?
faqs.answer: They end October 16 and December 17, 2026, and March 5 and May 14, 2027. The second, third and fourth periods begin October 19, January 4 and March 8. These are academic boundaries, not additional days off.

faqs.question: Which legal holidays have no student classes?
faqs.answer: Student holidays are July 3, 2026, for Independence Day observed; September 7 for Labor Day; November 11 for Veterans Day; November 26 for Thanksgiving; January 18, 2027, for Martin Luther King Jr. Day; February 15 for All Presidents Day; May 31 for Memorial Day; and June 18 for Juneteenth observed.

faqs.question: Does the school year end when the fourth grading period finishes?
faqs.answer: No. The fourth grading period and second semester end May 14, 2027, but Summer 2 begins May 17 and continues through June 29. The regular district’s June 3 last day is not this program’s endpoint.

faqs.question: Are employee opt days optional school days for students?
faqs.answer: No. The opt-day footnote concerns employee work arrangements. Teacher planning dates still state that no students are in school; the footnote does not make student attendance optional or designate weather make-up days.

faqs.question: Does the elementary Wednesday early-release schedule apply here?
faqs.answer: The Juvenile Justice Center PDF does not include that rule. The one-hour Wednesday release belongs to specified elementary and K-8 grades on a different calendar. Confirm this program’s daily schedule directly with the center.

faqs.question: Does this calendar cover all juvenile justice education programs in Florida?
faqs.answer: No. This is the calendar published by Miami-Dade County Public Schools for its Juvenile Justice Center. Other providers and programs may use a different schedule.

faqs.question: Where can families find daily class times and schedule updates?
faqs.answer: The annual PDF does not list daily start or dismissal times. Contact the center for the student’s schedule and program-specific arrangements, and use the district’s calendar page and official messages for changes.

editorialSummary.heading: Summer periods and Saturday classes are part of this year
paragraphs: The Juvenile Justice Center calendar follows a year-round pattern. Summer 1 begins July 2, 2026, and ends August 18, with the Independence Day observance on July 3 and three student-free planning days in August. The first semester then begins August 19. After the fourth grading period ends May 14, 2027, Summer 2 begins May 17 and continues through June 29. These summer periods belong to this program’s school year; families should use the center’s schedule when arranging appointments or checking attendance.

Fifteen Saturdays are listed as school days between August 22 and May 8. They are individual attendance dates, so an ordinary weekend assumption can lead to missed classes. Thanksgiving also differs from the regular district schedule: November 23 and 24 remain scheduled weekdays, followed by no student classes on the November 25 planning day, Thanksgiving Day and the November 27 recess. Winter Recess is December 21-January 1, with students also off December 18 and the third grading period beginning January 4. Spring Recess runs March 22-26, followed by a student-free planning day March 29.
highlights: The published program calendar totals 240 days.
Saturday classes are listed on 15 specific dates.
Summer 1 and Summer 2 each have 30 published days.
November 23-24 do not share the regular schools’ Fall Recess.
